turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. Owen found out about a zero from the online gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me. I have twenty minutes, so tell me why that zero is still there.
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski.
You asked for this meeting, Hale, so start. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent.
That's a machine's guess, Hale. The company that sells it says it shouldn't be the only basis for punishing a student. What else do you have?
That's very high. The software is quite reliable.
"Quite reliable." Procedure 4.3 in your own school's handbook says software results don't by themselves establish a concern. I asked what else you have, Hale, and I'm still waiting.
So I had to give him a zero.
"Had to." Under which rule, Hale? Procedure 4.1 says you speak with the student first, and 4.2 says you call me before any mark consequence is entered.
I hope you understand my position.
"I hope." I'm not here for your position, Hale, I'm here about the zero. Did anyone speak to Owen before it went into the gradebook, yes or no?
